name: Rilvegostomig
summary: Rilvegostomig (AZD2936) is AstraZeneca's monovalent PD-1/TIGIT bispecific IgG1 antibody, built on TIGIT antibodies licensed from Compugen in 2018. The lead programme is first-line NSCLC, three head-to-head Phase 3s against pembrolizumab with overall survival as the primary endpoint: ARTEMIDE-Lung04 (NCT06868277, monotherapy, PD-L1 high, 830 patients, primary completion 2030-01), ARTEMIDE-Lung02 (NCT06692738, squamous, with chemotherapy, 2030-07) and ARTEMIDE-Lung03 (NCT06627647, non-squamous, with chemotherapy, 2030-11), the two chemotherapy trials enrolling PD-L1 TC 1% or more. Price anchor: Keytruda, the comparator arm of all three, at $79,464 per CMS Part B beneficiary in 2024, the anchor the ABBV-1480 and PF-08634404 seeds use. Uptake anchor: pembrolizumab regimens made up at least 64.4% of US stage IV first-line therapy in 2015 to 2021 (Chen et al., Innov Pharm 2025), halved as a judgement. AstraZeneca pays Compugen tiered royalties of up to mid-single digits, netted in economics_share. Biliary tract and endometrial Phase 3s are not modelled: the book carries no biliary pool, and the lead indication is lung.

therapy_mode.source: ARTEMIDE-Lung02 (J Thorac Oncol 2025 abstract P3.18.35, jto.org/article/S1556-0864(25)02100-8/abstract) and ARTEMIDE-Lung03 (J Clin Oncol 2025;43(16_suppl):TPS8653, doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.16_suppl.TPS8653): rilvegostomig with platinum doublet every three weeks for 4 cycles, then rilvegostomig every three weeks (with pemetrexed maintenance in non-squamous); overall survival primary (book trials table for NCT06627647, NCT06692738, NCT06868277)
therapy_mode.note: Oncology treated to progression, so chronic by the house definition. Whether rilvegostomig is capped at a fixed number of cycles, as pembrolizumab is at 35, was not confirmed; the discontinuation rate is the controlling input either way
therapy_mode.check: Book trials table: NCT06627647, NCT06692738 and NCT06868277 all list overall survival as primary outcome, randomized, quadruple-blind. ARTEMIDE-Lung03 TPS8653 (JCO 2025, doi:10.1200/JCO.2025.43.16_suppl.TPS8653, seen via search): rilvegostomig plus pemetrexed-platinum q3w for 4 cycles, then rilvegostomig plus pemetrexed maintenance. ARTEMIDE-Lung02 (JTO P3.18.35): rilvegostomig plus carboplatin and paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel, then rilvegostomig. Treated to progression, so chronic. A cycle cap for rilvegostomig was not found either; the note says so.

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand Keytruda: CMS Medicare Part B 2024, $5,988,521,233 over 75,361 beneficiaries = $79,464 per beneficiary
list_price_per_patient.note: Judgement: house convention. Pembrolizumab is the comparator arm of ARTEMIDE-Lung02, -Lung03 and -Lung04 and is the PD-1 antibody rilvegostomig would replace; the ABBV-1480 and PF-08634404 seeds carry the same anchor. The case for lower: AstraZeneca's own Imfinzi reads $56,999 (Part B 2024), the anchor the volrustomig seed uses, and Merck expects US biosimilar competition to Keytruda from December 2028 and loss of European exclusivity in 2031 (Merck FY2025 10-K 0000310158-26-000063, risk factors, in the book's filing_sections), which would pull the reference price down before a 2032 first full year. The case for higher: a per-beneficiary figure covers less than a full year of therapy for many patients (adjuvant courses, deaths, stops), so it understates an annual price, and a new bispecific winning on overall survival could launch at a premium
list_price_per_patient.check: lookup.py demand Keytruda: Part B 2024 $5,988,521,233 / 75,361 beneficiaries = $79,464.46, so 0.079464 mm USD per patient-year. Pembrolizumab is the comparator arm of all three lung trials (book trial_interventions). Same anchor as the ABBV-1480 and PF-08634404 seeds (lookup.py seed). Imfinzi Part B 2024 reads $56,999, as the note says. Merck FY2025 10-K 0000310158-26-000063 risk factors in book filing_sections: 'biosimilar competition could begin in December 2028' and loss of exclusivity in Europe 'in 2031'. Labelled judgement with both cases.

gross_to_net_pct.source: house convention for a CMS Part B anchor (backend/gross_to_net.py): Part B pays 106% of average sales price, which is already net of manufacturer discounts and rebates (Social Security Act section 1847A), so only the 6% add-on comes off: 1 - 1/1.06. The volrustomig seed carries the same value on its Part B anchor
gross_to_net_pct.note: Direction checked: 0.056604 off list, so net is 0.079464 x 0.943396 = $74,966 per patient-year. Keytruda's beneficiaries sit in Part B (75,361 in 2024 against 1,906 in Part D), so the 0.5 Part D convention does not apply. The case against: ASP excludes Medicaid and 340B discounts, so the true net sits somewhat below this
gross_to_net_pct.check: Anchor is Part B (Keytruda 75,361 Part B beneficiaries against 1,906 Part D in 2024, lookup.py demand), so 1 - 1/1.06 = 0.056604 off list, which is the right direction. Net = 0.079464 / 1.06 = 0.074966, so $74,966. The volrustomig seed carries 0.056604 on its Part B anchor.

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: KEYNOTE-189 (Gandhi et al., N Engl J Med 2018;378:2078, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1801005, PMID 29658856): median PFS 8.8 months (95% CI 7.6 to 9.2) on pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum in untreated metastatic non-squamous NSCLC, the control regimen of ARTEMIDE-Lung03 (NCT06627647), the largest of the three lung trials at 1,160 patients
discontinuation_pct.note: Constant hazard from a median: 1 - 0.5^(12/8.8) = 0.611, the form the ABBV-1480, PF-08634404 and sigvotatug vedotin seeds use (the brief's 1 - exp(-12/8.8) gives 0.744 but treats the median as a mean). Judgement on which control arm: non-squamous is about 75% of known histology in the Chen et al. cohort (67.9% against 22.5%). The other two trials' control arms give 0.727 (KEYNOTE-407, squamous, median PFS 6.4 months, Paz-Ares et al., N Engl J Med 2018;379:2040, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1810865) and 0.554 (KEYNOTE-024, PD-L1 50% or more, 10.3 months, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1606774, the sigvotatug vedotin seed's source). The case for lower: the trials are designed to extend survival over pembrolizumab, and patients who respond stay on longer than the median implies; KEYNOTE-189's five-year update (Garassino et al., J Clin Oncol 2023;41:1992, doi:10.1200/JCO.22.01989) shows 57 of 410 completing all 35 cycles
discontinuation_pct.check: PubMed PMID 29658856: KEYNOTE-189 median PFS 8.8 months (95% CI 7.6 to 9.2) on pembrolizumab-combination. 1 - 0.5^(12/8.8) = 0.6114. PMID 30280635: KEYNOTE-407 median PFS 6.4 months, so 0.7274. KEYNOTE-024 at 10.3 months gives 0.5541, the verified sigvotatug vedotin seed's value. 1 - exp(-12/8.8) = 0.7443, as stated. PMID 36809080 (Garassino, JCO 2023;41:1992): 410 randomized to pembrolizumab-combination, 57 completed 35 cycles. Chen et al. histology split 67.9% vs 22.5%, so 75.1% non-squamous of known. The same constant-hazard form is used in the ABBV-1480 (11.1 mo), PF-08634404 (12.4 mo) and sigvotatug seeds. Minor wording point: Lung03 ties Lung02 at 1,160 patients and is not strictly 'the largest'. A histology-weighted blend (0.75 x 0.611 + 0.25 x 0.727 = 0.640) sits within the stated range. Labelled judgement.

forecast_start_year.source: book trials table (ClinicalTrials.gov): ARTEMIDE-Lung04 NCT06868277 primary completion 2030-01-17 (estimated), ARTEMIDE-Lung02 NCT06692738 2030-07-01, ARTEMIDE-Lung03 NCT06627647 2030-11-18; AstraZeneca Q1 2026 clinical trials appendix (astrazeneca.com/content/dam/az/PDF/2026/eq1/Q1-2026-results-clinical-trials-appendix.pdf) lists lung data as 2027+
forecast_start_year.note: Judgement: the book's convention of the first full year two calendar years after primary completion (the ABBV-1480 and PF-08634404 seeds), applied to Lung04, the first rilvegostomig-alone lung trial to complete: readout in 2030, filing in 2030 and approval around 2031. The chemotherapy trials that carry most of the pool complete later in 2030, so their labels would follow about a year after. The case for earlier: TROPION-Lung10 (NCT06357533), Datroway plus rilvegostomig against pembrolizumab in TROP2-positive, PD-L1-high non-squamous NSCLC, completes 2029-12-28, which the same convention would put at 2031, but it is a combination in a biomarker subset. Other indications complete earlier (adjuvant biliary NCT06109779 2029-01-02, DESTINY-Endometrial01 NCT06989112 2029-01-19) and are not modelled here
forecast_start_year.check: Book trials table: NCT06868277 primary completion 2030-01-17 (estimated), NCT06692738 2030-07-01, NCT06627647 2030-11-18, NCT06357533 2029-12-28, NCT06109779 2029-01-02, NCT06989112 2029-01-19. The ABBV-1480 seed (Dec 2029 to 2031) and PF-08634404 seed (Feb 2029 to 2031) put the first full year two calendar years after completion, so 2030-01 gives 2032. Search found the AstraZeneca Q1 2026 clinical trials appendix (29 April 2026) listing Lung02 (squamous, TC 1% or more), Lung03 (non-squamous, TC 1% or more) and Lung04 (PD-L1 50% or more). The '2027+' data timing was not shown in the search results and was not confirmed. It does not affect the value. Not mentioned by the researcher: NCT06564844 (TROPION-Lung12, adjuvant stage I NSCLC) has an actual primary completion of 2026-07-10 but only 25 enrolled, so no earlier label comes from it. NCT06467357 (HER2 biliary, 2028-06-12) is outside the modelled pool. TROPION-Lung10 missing the convention by three weeks (2029-12-28 would give 2031) is the stated case for earlier.

exus_multiple.source: Imfinzi FY2025 in the book's asset_revenue_regions (AstraZeneca 20-F 0001104659-26-019130, annual report table): US $3,509mm; Europe $1,239mm, Established ROW $675mm, Emerging Markets $640mm. (1,239 + 675 + 640) / 3,509 = 0.7278
exus_multiple.note: Judgement on the comparator: Imfinzi is AstraZeneca's own checkpoint antibody, sold worldwide by AstraZeneca, so its split reflects the company's IO footprint. The case against: Keytruda, the drug rilvegostomig would displace, reads 0.680 (Merck FY2025, $12,812mm non-US over $18,829mm US, book asset_revenue_regions), and Tagrisso, AstraZeneca's lung franchise, reads far higher because of Emerging Markets; a premium-priced bispecific may see slower ex-US reimbursement
exus_multiple.check: Book asset_revenue_regions, Imfinzi FY2025 (20-F 0001104659-26-019130 annual report table): US 3,509; Europe 1,239; Established ROW 675; Emerging Markets 640 ($mm; world 6,063 reconciles). (1,239 + 675 + 640) / 3,509 = 0.7278. Keytruda FY2025 NonUs 12,812 over US 18,829 = 0.6804, as the note says. Labelled judgement with case against.

economics_share.source: Compugen 6-K, 17 December 2025 (SEC accession 0001178913-25-004077, exhibit 99.1) and Compugen FY2025 20-F (0001178913-26-000663): under the March 2018 licence, AstraZeneca develops bispecifics from Compugen's TIGIT antibodies including COM902; on 16 December 2025 AstraZeneca bought part of the royalty for $65mm upfront plus $25mm added to the BLA-acceptance milestone, and Compugen 'remain[s] eligible for tiered royalties of up to mid-single digits on future sales' and up to $195mm in regulatory and commercial milestones. AstraZeneca cost rows from lookup.py seed Camizestrant or Volrustomig: cogs 0.181, SG&A 0.349206, R&D 0.2423, other costs -0.047173, so margin = 1 - 0.181 - 0.349206 - 0.2423 + 0.047173 = 0.274667
economics_share.note: Judgement on the rate: a royalty AstraZeneca pays, netted as (margin - royalty) / margin = (0.274667 - 0.05) / 0.274667 = 0.8180, reading 'up to mid-single digits' as 5% on the top tier where a large product's sales mostly fall. The exact tiers are not disclosed. At 4% the share is 0.8544, at 6% 0.7816. The case for a higher share: the royalty is tiered and 'up to', so early and lower-tier sales pay less. Milestones of up to $195mm to Compugen are not in this field. No other partner: AstraZeneca is lead sponsor of every rilvegostomig trial in the book
economics_share.check: Compugen royalty wording confirmed by search against the Compugen 6-K exhibit 99.1 (sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1119774/000117891325004077/exhibit_99-1.htm, the 17 Dec 2025 release; SEC itself is blocked here). The release says AstraZeneca paid '$65 million upfront payment and a potential additional $25 million upon the next milestone payment on BLA acceptance, for a portion of Compugen's existing royalty interest in rilvegostomig', and Compugen 'shall retain the majority of its future royalties and remain eligible for tiered royalties of up to mid-single digits on future sales and potential future regulatory and commercial milestones of up to $195 million (amount includes the $25 million stated above)'. AstraZeneca bought the royalty, so what Compugen keeps is AstraZeneca's remaining burden: up to mid-single-digit royalties is the right basis. The TIGIT arm derives from COM902. The March 2018 licence (Compugen FY2018 20-F) gave $10mm upfront, up to $200mm in milestones for the first product, and tiered royalties. AstraZeneca's filings in the book (only 6-K bodies from Sept 2026) do not mention Compugen or rilvegostomig. The FY2025 20-F accession 0001178913-26-000663 was not opened, but the 6-K alone supports the value. Arithmetic: AZN seed rows cogs 0.181, SG&A 0.349206, R&D 0.2423, other -0.047173 (lookup.py seed Volrustomig and Camizestrant), so margin = 0.274667. (0.274667 - 0.05) / 0.274667 = 0.8180; at 4% it is 0.8544 and at 6% 0.7816. This is the same margin-netting method as the PF-08634404 seed. All 25 rilvegostomig trials in the book have AstraZeneca as lead sponsor. Labelled judgement on 5%.

prevalence.source: carried by the book (epidemiology.csv: 192,650, SEER: 226,650 new US lung cancers in 2025, about 85% non-small cell)
prevalence.note: Carried by the book. Prevalence equals incidence on purpose, so the engine sets carryover to zero itself (backend/forecast.py) and no untreated_carryover_pct is stated
prevalence.check: lookup.py pool: epidemiology.csv carries Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung at 192,650, and eight seeds carry the same figure. Null is correct.

incidence.check: epidemiology.csv incidence 192,650, prevalence equal to incidence by the book's oncology convention. Null is correct.

eligible_pct.source: Four filters multiplied, each already in the book: 55% advanced or metastatic at presentation (the volrustomig seed); 81.6% without an alteration carrying a first-line targeted therapy (Wang et al., J Natl Compr Canc Netw 2026, doi:10.6004/jnccn.2025.7131, the PF-08634404 seed's share); 79% starting first-line therapy, 2,904 of 3,661 US stage IV patients without EGFR or ALK alterations (Abernethy et al., PLoS One 2017, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0178420, the ABBV-1480 seed's share); and 77.8% with PD-L1 of 1% or more, about 3,770 of 4,848 first-line-treated US patients with a quantified result (Leapman et al., JAMA Netw Open 2020;3(6):e207205, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2020.7205, PMID 32511721, the PF-08046054 seed's share). 0.55 x 0.816 x 0.79 x 0.778 = 0.2758, about 53,100 patients a year
eligible_pct.note: The label union of the three lung trials: Lung02 and Lung03 enrol squamous and non-squamous first-line metastatic NSCLC with PD-L1 TC 1% or more (J Thorac Oncol 2025 P3.18.35; J Clin Oncol 2025 TPS8653), and Lung04 enrols PD-L1 high, a subset of that. PD-L1-negative patients (about 22%) are outside every trial. The case against: the driver filter is applied to squamous tumours too, where actionable alterations are rare, which slightly understates; the 55% counts only advanced disease at presentation and misses recurrence after early-stage treatment, which also understates; and PD-L1 status and driver status are not independent, which cuts the other way
eligible_pct.check: 0.55 x 0.816 x 0.79 x 0.778 = 0.27584, x 192,650 = 53,141 a year. Each filter is on a book seed: 55% (volrustomig), 81.6% Wang et al. (PF-08634404, sigvotatug), and 79% Abernethy 2,904/3,661 (ABBV-1480, PF-08634404; 0.7932 unrounded). 77.8%: PubMed PMID 32511721 (Leapman) gives PD-L1 high 1,541 = 83.5%, low 776 = 40.3%, negative 348 = 32.3%. Back-solved denominators are 1,846 + 1,926 + 1,077 = 4,848, and 3,772 / 4,848 = 0.778 (PF-08046054 seed). The label union is confirmed by search: Lung02 squamous TC 1% or more (JTO P3.18.35), Lung03 non-squamous TC 1% or more (TPS8653), and Lung04 PD-L1 50% or more (AZ Q1 2026 appendix), all first line, locally advanced or metastatic. The stated cases against are reasonable.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of each year's eligible patients
penetration_peak_pct.source: Pembrolizumab, the incumbent: in 8,811 US patients with advanced NSCLC starting treatment 2015 to 2021, the five most common first-line regimens in stage IV, 64.4% of all first-line therapy, were all pembrolizumab alone or with platinum chemotherapy (Chen et al., Innov Pharm 2025;16(3), doi:10.24926/iip.v16i3.6702, PMID 42256417, the paper the ABBV-1480 seed uses for histology). 0.644 x 0.5 = 0.322
penetration_peak_pct.note: Judgement: half the incumbent's measured share, the multiple the verified sigvotatug vedotin seed takes. Rilvegostomig is a like-for-like swap for pembrolizumab in the same regimens, so pembrolizumab's share is its ceiling if it wins on overall survival. The case for higher: 64.4% is a floor, since it counts only the top five regimens, includes driver-positive patients treated with targeted drugs, and averages in 2015 and 2016 before first-line approval; Leapman et al. found 83.5% of PD-L1-high first-line patients received an ICI by 2016 to 2018. The case for lower: the slot will be crowded by 2032, with PD-1/VEGF bispecifics (ivonescimab, PF-08634404, ABBV-1480), AstraZeneca's own volrustomig in PD-L1 below 50%, and pembrolizumab biosimilars from December 2028 (Merck FY2025 10-K 0000310158-26-000063), which make the incumbent cheap just as rilvegostomig launches; and the anti-TIGIT mechanism has no approved precedent, so even an overall survival win may meet caution. The book's other first-line lung seeds (volrustomig, PF-08634404, ABBV-1480) carry 0.2 without a measured anchor. Case lower, from the second reader: if rilvegostomig does not beat pembrolizumab and AstraZeneca mostly switches its own checkpoint patients, the capture is 0.02 (Imjudo's 1,259 Part B beneficiaries over the 53,141 eligible) to 0.13 (pembrolizumab's share scaled by the Imfinzi franchise against Keytruda); the probability of success already carries that failure case, so 0.322 is the peak if it wins
penetration_peak_pct.check: Input: PubMed (Chen et al., Innov Pharm 2025, doi:10.24926/iip.v16i3.6702) says 'In stage IV patients, the five most common LoT1, comprising 64.4% of all LoT1, were pembrolizumab either as monotherapy or combined with other platinum-based chemotherapeutic agents' (8,811 advanced NSCLC, 2015 to 2021). 0.644 x 0.5 = 0.322. The half multiple matches the verified sigvotatug vedotin seed (0.51 x 0.5 = 0.255). Leapman 83.5% is confirmed. The share uses the same first-line-treated basis as the pool. IMFINZI-SWITCH TEST (asked for): if rilvegostomig mostly moves AstraZeneca's own Imfinzi patients, there is almost nothing to move in this pool. Imfinzi's first-line metastatic NSCLC regimen (POSEIDON, with Imjudo, approved Nov 2022) is capped by Imjudo's Part B 2024 total of 1,259 beneficiaries (lookup.py demand), which also counts HCC. 1,259 / 53,141 = 0.024 of the eligible pool, Medicare only. Chen et al.'s top five stage IV regimens (2015 to 2021) were all pembrolizumab. Even scaling pembrolizumab's share by Imfinzi's whole franchise against Keytruda's (14,791 / 75,361 Part B beneficiaries = 0.196) gives only 0.644 x 0.196 = 0.126. So the switch case implies about 0.02 to 0.13, not 0.322. It is the scenario in which rilvegostomig does not displace pembrolizumab. All three lung trials test it against pembrolizumab with OS primary, and the engine prices failure through its own probability of success, so a peak conditional on an OS win is the right input. The switch case belongs mainly to biliary (ARTEMIDE-Biliary02 against durvalumab, not modelled) and to Imfinzi's stage III and perioperative lung use, which is outside this first-line metastatic pool. Cannibalisation of Imfinzi inside this pool is at most about 0.024, about 7% of the 0.322 peak. The note's case for lower does not name the switch case, and a reader should add it. The value stands as a labelled judgement on confirmed inputs. | Assembler: the switch case the second reader measured was added to the note

ramp_steepness.source: book: Enhertu's CMS Part B launch fit (864, 1,904, 4,841, 7,105, 8,410 beneficiaries 2020 to 2024), k = 1.08, midpoint 2.2 years, as carried by the volrustomig, PF-08634404, ABBV-1480 and sigvotatug vedotin seeds
ramp_steepness.note: Reused measured oncology curve, so the first-line lung seeds ramp alike
ramp_steepness.check: lookup.py demand Enhertu Part B beneficiaries 864, 1,904, 4,841, 7,105, 8,410 (2020 to 2024). The volrustomig, PF-08634404, ABBV-1480 and sigvotatug seeds all carry k = 1.08 and midpoint 2.2. The logistic at those values gives 0.10, 0.25, 0.51, 0.80, 1.00 of the 2024 level against observed 0.10, 0.23, 0.58, 0.84, 1.00.

ramp_midpoint_year.source: as ramp_steepness (Enhertu fit carried in the book)
ramp_midpoint_year.note: Reused. The case for later: the chemotherapy-combination labels, most of the pool, likely follow the Lung04 monotherapy label by about a year, which a shift of up to one year would reflect
ramp_midpoint_year.check: Same Enhertu fit, midpoint 2.2 years, carried by the four named seeds. The note's case for later (chemotherapy-combination labels about a year after Lung04) is consistent with the confirmed primary completions (2030-01 against 2030-07 and 2030-11).
